title: SEED-13 consumer-side root cause: neither memory-awareness's skip list nor extractIntent has any machine-content guard or length cap — XML/markdown blobs >=15 chars pass straight through as recall intents, get logged raw, and ride the full hybrid recall (~12s budget)
causal_links: seed SEED-13 (<task-notification> XML blobs as recall intents) — this is the missing guard that lets them through
amplified-by D3c-03 (gitExpanded bypass skips even the meta-language stripping)
same gap in agent-recall-injector: extractIntent over a multi-KB agent prompt yields the whole prompt as --query argv (see D3c-01 telemetry sample)
observe_how: The only skips before recall are: CLAUDE_AGENT_ID set, prompt<15 chars, leading '/'. META_PATTERNS in intent-extractor.ts strip only human meta-language ('can you', 'how do i', ...). A prompt beginning '<task-notification>' or '## Mode' passes both gates verbatim; intent is stored uncapped in memory-recall.jsonl (capped at 200 chars only at the injection surface) and in Braintrust metadata.intent.
telemetry: Harvest: intent_pollution 24.6% (69/281 rows). Fix candidates: reject/strip intents starting with '<' or markdown-heading structure, cap intent length before logging/querying, and skip system-generated UserPromptSubmit events. Each polluted intent burns the full 12s hybrid (or 5s text-only) recall budget for a structurally unmatchable query.

title: Live codegraph queries run 35-50s (telemetry-verified), 10x the documented 3-4s budget: ensureFresh spawns one full codegraph process per dirty/untracked file, on EVERY call, with no source-file filter

evidence.quote: Each codegraph call pays a ~3-4s Node+WASM startup tax — amortized by the freshness cache, never by making codegraph faster.

causal_links: SEED-09
telemetry: All 37 live codegraph rows in .claude/logs/intel-bus.jsonl show duration_ms 34875-49979 (sampled: 34875, 39636, 49979, 40551, 44525, 42250). The boundary contract calls codegraph 'broad, fast, FTS-first'.
observe_how: With 3+ dirty/untracked files (any extension - .md/.json count too), time `node scripts/code-intel.mjs find-symbol Foo` and count spawned codegraph node processes. Each dirty file = one ~3-8s process spawn, re-paid on every facade call because _freshnessDone/_gitHeadCache are per-process and each CLI call is a new process; only the .indexed-head stamp persists, and it only tracks HEAD, not worktree dirt. Note syncWholeProject already does the same work in ONE spawn ('sync -q root'), so the per-file loop is strictly worse whenever dirty count > 1; worst case is 200 spawns (~13+ min). The rule's 'amortized by the freshness cache' claim is disproven by the live durations.

title: SEED-01 culprit NAMED: agent-error-capture.ts builds a shell command string from un-sanitized agent error output (escapes only " and \n), redirecting store_learning.py stdout into junk files like opc/400`
causal_links: causes SEED-01
caused-by same shell-string pattern as D5a-02
sibling of D5a-03
observe_how: The quarantined junk artifact's content is verbatim store_learning.py stdout (`~ Learning skipped: noise_prefix: Agent '`). store_learning.py emits that EXACT string only when content begins with the prefix "Agent '" (NOISE_PREFIXES). The only code in the repo that builds content starting with "Agent '" is agent-error-capture.ts:144. agent-error-capture is registered PostToolUse:Task in active settings.json. When a Task agent's tool_response matches an ERROR_PATTERN, the hook execs a SHELL string (execSync runs through cmd.exe on Windows) interpolating the agent's raw error text, escaped only for double-quote and newline. Shell metacharacters in the agent output (backtick, >, <, |, &, ;) pass through live -> a `>` in the error text redirected store_learning.py's stdout into a file named by the adjacent token (e.g. `400` / `Safety` with a trailing backtick), creating the junk files. Re-confirm trigger via Task Scheduler shows no daily task spawns agents at 07:24 -> trigger is a logon-time interactive session (INFERRED); the call-site bug is the root cause (VERIFIED).
telemetry: Count files matching ^opc/[^/]*`$ (junk artifacts); add a stderr canary when escapedContent contains any of ` $ ( ) > < | ; & before execSync.
